answer: A timber yard on a windy ridge gives each agent one numbered stack to tend. Each morning the yard keeper reads the zephyr and calls out its speed and direction, and every keeper ties a signal tag to the top beam of their own stack with that reading and the stack count. A second keeper walks the yard at dusk, checks each tag against the wind log, and drops any stack whose tag is missing or wrong. A thousand fake names need a thousand stacks of real timber, each tagged by hand in the same morning wind window, each with its own keeper at the gate.
